beats.headline: In a dusty corner
beats.text: Limp Richard's general store sells nothing much worth having; Donut talks a padded mallet down from 250 gold to 150. In a dusty corner stands a thing called a Battery Fabricator, about the size of a microwave, listed at 75,000 gold. The shop's own description admits it does not really know how the thing works: taken from a dwarven automaton factory, mana potions in, a metal block in, a charged battery out, a box of fifty batteries included, price not negotiable. Each battery is about the size and weight of a brick. The system will not give a real description until it is bought. Carl wants it on sight and cannot justify the price.

beats.headline: Traded for westerns and moonshine
beats.text: Pulling the battery from a railway cart, Carl recognises it: a dwarven battery, at two percent. He has the fabricator now, traded for the rest of his westerns and a single jug of moonshine; the mole man practically begged, having finished the books Carl had already given him. Carl suspected the fabricator's odd placement in the first store they came to was no coincidence. The cookbook says each battery takes four full mana potions to charge, and it takes five minutes. Fifty came with it, most at ten to fifteen percent, five full and five at half; Carl charged two more, for twelve usable. If every powered cart here has one, that is another forty-plus for the stash.

relations.note: Its carts run on dwarven batteries
